Hi Sofia / Ben,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Astera is ready to move forward on renewal but we have three items we need captured in the paperwork before procurement will sign:

1) Term: we are requesting a 36-month term (was previously 24) in exchange for the expanded commitment.
2) Capacity: increase committed tokens from 1,000,000/mo to 3,000,000/mo (Order Form change).
3) Liability & data: limited changes to data retention (90 days for logs) and liability cap — procurement is asking for 2x annual fees instead of 1x.

I've attached our redline (Astera_Renewal_Redline_20280714.docx) and the latest order form (Astera_OrderForm_v3.pdf) with inline highlights. Procurement wants to close before month-end; please advise if the liability cap and data retention asks are deal-breakers.

Also: we need a clear signature path (DocuSign preferred).

Best,
Elena

Subject: Re: Renewal packet: term adjustment + capacity increase — legal redlines

Sofia / Ben — quick read and high level:

- Term/Capacity: no legal objection to a 36-month term and the order-form capacity increase; commercial should confirm pricing and SKUs.
- Liability cap: standard Redwood position is aggregate liability capped at 1x annual fees (except for breach of IP and gross negligence). Moving to 2x is material. If Sales wants to concede, we should trade: (a) stronger SLA credits (higher cap on credits) OR (b) a carve-out limiting increased cap to data loss / confidentiality breach only.
- Data retention: 90 days for logs is acceptable for product logs, but production-level customer data (PII) requires our standard 180-day archival retention unless we switch to customer-managed retention and a tighter access control plan.
- Indemnity language: Astera's redline adds a broader third-party claim indemnity for customer-provided models. We need to limit indemnity to Redwood's direct breach and to require customer to (i) warrant they have rights to customer-provided models and (ii) defend first.

Suggested next steps: attached RW_Legal_Suggested_20280715.pdf containing strike-and-insert language for the order form and MSA. If Sales is willing to offer a pricing concession or stronger SLA terms, I can support a one-off liability cap increase limited to the renewal term.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: RW_Legal_Suggested_20280715.pdf

Sofia / Kimberly — pricing note: 1M -> 3M committed tokens increases annual committed spend from $360k to $980k at standard list. For 36 months we can offer a stepped discount schedule that lands effective ARR at ~28% lower than list vs a 24-month renewal. If we accommodate a 2x liability cap we should offset with a 5% increase to list price or require the stronger SLA credits Kimberly mentioned.

I've drafted an updated order form (Astera_OrderForm_v4.xlsx) with the 3M commitment and the stepped discount; see the redlines in the Pricing tab.

Procurement path: send OrderForm_v4 + MSA (with legal's suggested language) to DocuSign. If procurement wants a blanket 2x cap across all liability categories we should escalate to VP Sales (Marissa) for approval.

Thanks Sofia / Ben / Kimberly — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from procurement:

• The 2x liability cap is non-negotiable for them unless we provide an explicit SLA-credit ladder that caps their downside if Redwood misses SLOs. They asked for a schedule that yields up to 25% credit on sustained SLA misses.
• For data retention, Astera is willing to accept the 180-day archival for PII if Redwood agrees to an annual third-party audit (SOC-type evidence) limited to controls around access and deletion.

I've attached a signed procurement acknowledgement for internal processing (Procurement_approval_signed.pdf). We still need: final MSA language and a DocuSign envelope ready for signatures.

Goal: get to DocuSign by EOD Friday.

Elena

4) DocuSign: I will upload the final MSA + OrderForm_v4 to DocuSign and share the envelope link once legal confirms the text. Target: envelope sent by EOD Friday.
